headline: Sea temperature at Rockall hits an August record for the third year running
standfirst: The buoy has been on station since 1978. The three warmest readings in its history have all come since 2024.

image.alt: A weather buoy in heavy swell under grey sky

body.text: The Rockall buoy is not glamorous. It is a yellow cylinder in a bad piece of ocean, and it has been returning the same measurements on the same schedule for forty-eight years. That consistency is precisely what makes this month's figure difficult to argue with.
Surface temperature peaked at 16.8°C on 29 July, three-tenths above the 2025 record and a full 1.9°C above the 1978–2008 baseline for the date.
A record is interesting. A record that keeps being broken by the same margin is a trend.

The practical consequence is northward range shift. Species that were rare north of the Porcupine Bank a decade ago are now routine in survey hauls, and the species that used to be there are running out of north.
